tldr: Fast ECoT accelerates Embodied Chain-of-Thought reasoning by caching reusable high-level reasoning across timesteps, parallelizing reasoning step generation, and using an asynchronous scheduler to decouple reasoning from action decoding, achieving up to 7.7× latency reduction without model changes or additional training.
contributions: Proposing Fast ECoT, an inference-time acceleration method exploiting structured temporal locality in ECoT reasoning
Caching and reusing high-level reasoning segments (e.g., planning, subtasks) across timesteps based on low update ratios
Parallelizing modular reasoning step generation using continuous batching via vLLM
Introducing an asynchronous scheduler that decouples slow reasoning updates from fast action decoding
Demonstrating improvements in both simulation (LIBERO) and real-world robot tasks
methods: The authors analyzed ECoT reasoning patterns on Bridge V2 and LIBERO-Goal, finding that high-level reasoning components like planning have low update ratios (e.g., 8.4%), meaning ~92% of content is reusable across timesteps. They reformulated each reasoning step as an independent generation task using prior context as prefix, enabling parallel generation. Continuous batching via vLLM handles variable-length inputs efficiently. An asynchronous mechanism allows the controller to decode actions from cached high-level reasoning while reasoning traces update in the background.
results: In LIBERO simulation, Fast ECoT achieves 80.0% average success rate (highest among all methods) with 2156±353 ms latency (2.3× faster than ECoT's 4997±691 ms). Fast ECoT (Async) reaches 686±412 ms (nearly 7× faster) with 77.5% success rate and best LIBERO-Long performance (69%). In real-world experiments, Fast ECoT achieves 68.3% average success rate, while Fast ECoT (Async) delivers 716±529 ms latency (7.7× speedup over ECoT's 5556±384 ms) with 65.3% average success rate.
limitations: Fast ECoT (Async) shows sensitivity to object layouts, with reduced performance on LIBERO-Object (75% vs 83% for standard Fast ECoT)
Async reasoning introduces temporal mismatch between cached reasoning and rapidly evolving actions
Prior ECoT variants either sacrifice task performance or suffer high inference latency
Low-level reasoning components refresh more frequently, limiting reuse opportunities for those steps
